property_summary: After any valid fallback call, pastBlockTime is always strictly less than the current block timestamp.
After any fallback call with msg.value = 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the new pastBlockTime is at least 1 greater than the previous pastBlockTime.
After a successful fallback call that triggers the transfer, pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the previous pastBlockTime.

After any successful fallback call, the stored pastBlockTime plus the block's timestamp offset remains at least 1; the mutant which sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp violates this invariant when two consecutive calls occur at the same timestamp.
After any two consecutive fallback calls at the same timestamp, pastBlockTime must be greater than the first call's timestamp.
After a call to fallback() with msg.value == 10 ether, pastBlockTime (the timestamp of the last successful call) is strictly greater than the block.timestamp of any previous call that modified it.

A call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether always increments pastBlockTime to at least block.timestamp + 1, ensuring pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the previous block.timestamp after each successful call.

After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether that sets pastBlockTime, the next call with the same msg.value at the same block.timestamp must revert (proving strict inequality enforcement).
pastBlockTime strictly increases after every successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether
After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, pastBlockTime is always greater than the block.timestamp at the time of the call.
After any call to the fallback function, pastBlockTime is always equal to block.timestamp + 1, regardless of whether the transfer in the if-block reverted.
After a successful fallback call, pastBlockTime equals block.timestamp + 1
After any even/odd block-number call, pastBlockTime always equals block.timestamp + 1, regardless of whether the if-block transfer happened.
After any fallback call, pastBlockTime is always greater than the previous pastBlockTime, not just equal to block.timestamp + 1.
After a call to the fallback function that does not trigger the if-block (block.number % 15 != 0), pastBlockTime is set to block.timestamp + 1.
After any call to fallback with 10 ether, if block.number % 15 != 0 then the contract balance remains unchanged.
After calling the fallback function with exactly 10 ether and valid timestamp, the contract's balance should decrease by exactly 10 ether when block.number % 15 == 0.
After a failed fallback call that reverts due to invalid timestamp, the contract's pastBlockTime must remain unchanged.
When the fallback is called with 10 ether and block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance decrease equals the amount transferred to msg.sender.
After each fallback call with 10 ether, the contract's balance always changes by at least the value sent (10 ether) regardless of block number condition.
After calling fallback with 10 ether when block.number % 15 == 0, the contract balance decreases by exactly the amount transferred to msg.sender.
After calling fallback with 10 ether, the contract balance does not increase by 10 ether (i.e., the sent ether is not retained).
After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether after a successful prior call, the contract balance is always 10 ether or less (i.e., the if-block's ether-sending is not executed).
After any sequence of calls to c.fallback, the contract balance never decreases below 0 (i.e., the ether-sending if-block never executes).
After a sequence of two fallback calls with 10 ether at increasing timestamps, the contract balance reflects the cumulative deposits without any transfers.
The contract balance never decreases after a fallback call with exactly 10 ether.
